database-unreachable.AlarmDescription: Something ran and could not reach the database. A zero here is a different incident from a gap: the gap means nothing ran.

job-failures-elevated.AlarmDescription: Retries are burning attempt budget. Read the scrubbed last_error on the affected rows; do not read payloads.

job-poisoned.AlarmDescription: Work has been abandoned. Nothing will retry it. Decide whether to fix and requeue or to drop it, and record which.

outbox-undelivered.AlarmDescription: Somebody was promised a message half an hour ago. The relay is at-least-once, so re-running cannot lose one.

queue-backlog.AlarmDescription: Depth alone is not an incident. Check queue-oldest-age first; a deep queue that is draining needs nothing.

queue-oldest-age.AlarmDescription: A job has waited half an hour. This is the backlog signal that matters; depth is context for it.

schedule-overdue.AlarmDescription: Materialization has stopped while the worker kept looping. The slot key is deterministic, so re-running is safe.

worker-heartbeat-stale.AlarmDescription: No worker has checked in for fifteen minutes. Unlike worker-stopped this survives the publisher dying, because any surviving process reports the newest heartbeat it can see.

worker-live-but-not-claiming.AlarmDescription: Ticks are arriving and nothing is being claimed. Compare against queue_depth: zero depth means genuinely idle, non-zero depth means claiming is broken (lease contention, a provider permit held open, or a tenant filter).

worker-stopped.AlarmDescription: The loop is not running. Check the host and the container state before anything else -- every other alarm below is downstream of this one.
